Method
• Support the plastic cup in a 250 cm beaker.

• Tilt the beaker so that the bulb of the thermometer is covered by the solution.
• Measure and record the temperature of the solution.

• Carefully tip all the hydrated sodium carbonate from the weighed tube into the
plastic cup.

to the beaker.
• Stir with a glass rod until all the solid has dissolved.
• Pour the solution from the beaker into the 250 cm graduated (volumetric) flask.

graduated flask.
• Make up the contents of the graduated flask to the 250 cm mark with distilled
water.
• Shake the flask to mix the solution of FB 1.
• Pipette 25.0 cm of your solution of FB 1 into a conical flask.
• Add to the flask a few drops of methyl orange indicator and place the flask on a
white tile.
• Fill the burette with hydrochloric acid, FB 2.
• Titrate the solution of FB 1 with the acid until the end-point is reached.
